title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space sector is bustling with activity as governments and private firms alike prioritize resilience and security in orbit. Notably, funding continues to flow into space ventures, while the race for space traffic management intensifies amidst rising geopolitical tensions.

themes.title: Space Security Spending Surge
themes.body: Governments are increasingly recognizing the need for robust space security, with the global SSA market projected to hit $61 billion. This trend is underscored by a $1.4 billion boost in the FY27 budget dedicated to enhancing space resilience.

themes.title: Traffic Management Takes Center Stage
themes.body: As orbital congestion becomes a pressing issue, the importance of establishing an equilibrium state for space traffic management is gaining traction. This could pave the way for new regulatory frameworks and technologies to ensure safer operations in crowded orbits.

themes.title: Funding Flows into Space Ventures
themes.body: Impulse Space's recent $500 million raise and True Anomaly's $190 million Series C highlight the growing investor appetite for space-related technologies. This influx of capital suggests that the space economy is maturing, attracting serious players with deep pockets.

themes.title: Geopolitical Tensions in Orbit
themes.body: With reports of Russian co-orbital activities near commercial GEO slots, the stakes for space security are rising. This development signals a potential escalation in the competition for strategic advantages in space, further complicating the landscape for satellite operators.
